name: Executive order of December 31, 1873 amending the Santee (Niobrara) reservation order of August 31, 1869
promises: Not a treaty. Royce says the order only excepted from the lands added to the reserve in 1869 lots 1 to 4 of section 3, T. 32 [33?] N., R. 4 W., which had been patented to Thomas J. Quinn, a tract too small to map.
Royce's area 556 is the Santee or Niobrara reserve as it then stood.
today: No court or claims finding about this order was located. Royce notes that the executive order of February 9, 1885 restored unallotted Santee reservation lands to the public domain; that order has its own record.

sources.title: Charles C. Royce, Indian Land Cessions in the United States (18th Annual Report of the Bureau of American Ethnology, 1899), schedule pp. 868-869

openQuestions: The ICC title search for "santee" returns only the Sioux Nation (Black Hills) dockets.
The township of the excepted lots is printed by Royce as "T. 32 [33?] N."; left as printed.
